question: Does changing the complete unclaimed HEADER suffix affect this ODA conversion of the AC1027 Cover resave?

source.description: ODA File Converter 27.1.0 same-revision AC1027 resave of the local Cover drawing, from the previous same-version resave receipt

method.procedure: The suffix is a unique contiguous literal in this compressed page. Make two scratch copies: replace all 739 bytes with zero or with byte (73*index+19) modulo 256. Recompute the compressed-page data and encrypted-header checksums, leaving all other physical bytes and the HEADER sentinel, declared length and CRC unchanged.
method.localDecode: The existing dwgReader27 section probe reads both modified sections, verifies the page checksums, and shows that all 844 bytes through the HEADER ending sentinel are byte-identical to the source; the 739-byte suffix matches each replacement.
method.independentDecode: LibreDWG 0.14 decompress_R2004_section independently reproduces all 1583 logical bytes for both modified pages; its remaining output-window bytes are outside this comparison.
method.controls: The mutation tool reproduces both scratch DWG hashes, refuses an invalid original page checksum, and exclusively creates output rather than overwriting an existing file.

converter.executable: ODA File Converter 27.1.0 native macOS ARM64, verified outside sandbox
converter.operation: ACAD2013 DXF; recursion 0; audit 0; original and both copies in one input directory
converter.result: All three files yielded DXF without .err. The only line differences are the values following $TDUPDATE and $TDUUPDATE. Replacing just those values by a common marker produces the same 127131-byte SHA-256 6fed5d4bb382c358a5e6a7a051bc1667cb2ec41929d58e87a65adbacb61b2d52 for all three DXFs.

originalCoverRepeat.source: Original AC1027 Cover.dwg, SHA-256 3a6c23151ebec25320722f0ecaaf20a10073c60079d3616181395f1c73deee42; producer provenance is not independently established.
originalCoverRepeat.framing: The 731-byte suffix starts after the validated HEADER trailer at decoded offset 844 and occurs as one literal at physical offset 0x434f in the compressed page beginning at 0x40a0.
originalCoverRepeat.verification: Both checksum-valid mutations decode with the same first 844 HEADER bytes, and LibreDWG independently matches both full 1575-byte logical sections.
originalCoverRepeat.odaResult: The same ODA ACAD2013 DXF route converts original and both variants without .err. With only $TDUPDATE and $TDUUPDATE values normalized, all three DXFs have 127131 bytes and SHA-256 721bce02dec30f9cc78d2c20b6dee2671b9329b904ee8d191e9d4ac33680dc1a.

ac1018EtBorderRepeat.source: ODA AC1018-to-AC1018 resave of the local ET Border drawing, SHA-256 99f261cf43273013e3cac4182abd2acf34f7a1679acab28d26ab34f34eb9e94d; see the AC1018 suffix diagnostic receipt.
ac1018EtBorderRepeat.framing: The 739-byte suffix begins after validated HEADER trailer offset 534 in the 1273-byte logical section. Its unique contiguous literal begins at physical offset 0x9364; the compressed page begins at 0x9180.
ac1018EtBorderRepeat.verification: LibreDWG independently decompresses both modified pages. The original 534-byte HEADER envelope is unchanged and each suffix matches its replacement.
ac1018EtBorderRepeat.odaResult: ODA ACAD2004 DXF converts the source and both variants without .err. After normalizing only $TDUPDATE and $TDUUPDATE values, all three DXFs have 255429 bytes and SHA-256 41680914f9d58706af445291c72388183af7371c26701010a58c111aae8fbf8b.

limits: This is a causal comparison of two drawings across AC1018 and AC1027 through one converter; it does not identify a suffix generator or prove suffixes are padding for other sources or consumers.
ODA's own DXF projection may omit information; equal DXF bytes after timestamp normalization are not native semantic equivalence or full drawing preservation.
Strict output continues to refuse unclaimed suffixes, and no support or parity claim is promoted. No drawing fixture is committed.
next: Repeat on independent producer/version profiles and native semantic routes, and establish a source-backed admission rule before changing strict output.
